newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil portworkers strike stops loading activity.
newsitem.headline: Brazil portworkers strike stops loading activity.

text.p: These are the conditions at major Brazilian ports on Nov 26, after the National Portworker's Federation called a nationwide 24-hour strike to protest a bill regulating inland and coastal shipping.

* Santos - The port is virtually stopped. There are 42 ships at Santos but only three ships containing chemical products are loading and unloading. Cargo movement on ships carrying sugar, wheat and orange juice has been halted, port authorities said.

* Vitoria - There are six ships at the port but only one ship carrying fruit has been able to load. Operations in the remaining five ships carrying rice, cotton, pulp, malt and containers has been halted, a spokesman for the port said.
* Paranagua - There are eleven ships at the port but authorities were unable to provide information on cargo movement.
* Rio de Janeiro - No information available. Port authorities said the strike affected only stevedores and loading teams. They said the strike is expected to end Wednesday at 0700 local/0900 gmt.
